name: ro-array-core-mc-freq
description: Monte Carlo device mismatch on the shipped 2-ring x 11-stage entropy-source array (design/ro_array_core.spice): per-ring period/current spread across virtual chip samples, at the nominal corner. Issue #13's RO-frequency-spread MC run.
tstep: 1p (print step; ngspice's own LTE sets the actual solver step)
analyses: meas tran t1a when v(xdut.ro1)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran t1b when v(xdut.ro1)=v(vth) rise=6
meas tran t2a when v(xdut.ro2)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran t2b when v(xdut.ro2)=v(vth) rise=6
meas tran c1a find v(q1) when v(xdut.ro1)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran c1b find v(q1) when v(xdut.ro1)=v(vth) rise=6
meas tran c2a find v(q2) when v(xdut.ro2)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran c2b find v(q2) when v(xdut.ro2)=v(vth) rise=6
caveats: Nominal corner only (tt/27C/3.30V). gf180mcu's `statistical` library section supplies intra-die mismatch on top of whichever corner's devices are loaded; this run does not repeat the mismatch draw at ff/ss or at temperature/supply extremes, so it says nothing about whether mismatch spread widens or narrows at those corners.

8 mismatch seeds is enough to characterize the spread's rough magnitude, not to bound a tail probability -- a claim about the FRACTION of parts that would violate the non-integer-ratio requirement needs many more samples than this record provides.

Each seed is an independent full-array mismatch draw (both rings, the XOR gate, everything in design/ro_array_core.spice redrawn together), which is the physically correct picture for one chip -- but it means the two rings' mismatch draws are correlated only through whatever global (not per-device) variation `sw_stat_global` would add, which this testbench leaves off (sw_stat_mismatch=1, sw_stat_global=0 default): local/intra-die mismatch only, no die-to-die global corner spread on top of the tt corner already selected.
